Dear Neuromuscular Specialist,

As a specialist managing adults with anti–AChR antibody–positive generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG), we wanted to share the latest clinical data on a long-acting complement option for your appropriate patients.

A long-acting complement option for appropriate adults with anti‑AChR+ gMG

ULTOMIRIS® (ravulizumab-cwvz) is indicated for adults with anti–AChR antibody–positive gMG. In the randomized CHAMPION‑MG trial, ULTOMIRIS demonstrated clinically meaningful control of the symptom journey over 26 weeks — with a convenient every‑8‑weeks IV maintenance regimen.1

More than 2x greater MG‑ADL improvement vs placebo at Week 26

In the randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled CHAMPION‑MG trial (ULTOMIRIS n=86; placebo n=89), ULTOMIRIS achieved a statistically significant, greater mean improvement in MG‑ADL total score at Week 26 vs placebo.2

Improvements in MG‑ADL were observed as early as Week 1 and were sustained through the 26‑week treatment period, with most patients continuing background gMG therapies.2

Clinician-assessed muscle strength: significant QMG improvements at 26 weeks

At Week 26, ULTOMIRIS demonstrated significant improvements in clinician-assessed global muscle strength vs placebo on the Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) scale.3

Exploratory analyses reported additional QMG domain-level improvements across ocular, bulbar, and limb domains.3

Immediate, complete, and sustained terminal complement C5 inhibition through 26 weeks

ULTOMIRIS is the first and only long‑acting complement C5 inhibitor indicated for anti‑AChR+ gMG.4

<0.5 µg/mL

Serum free C5 achieved in all treated adults by the end of the initial infusion, and maintained through 26 weeks — supporting every‑8‑weeks IV maintenance dosing.4

PK/PD data support weight‑based loading followed by maintenance dosing Q8W. No direct efficacy or safety conclusions are drawn solely from PK/PD analyses.4

Safety profile and meningococcal risk considerations with ULTOMIRIS

In adults with gMG receiving ULTOMIRIS across the randomized and open‑label periods, the most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were:5

Adverse Reaction (≥10%)All-grade incidence
Diarrhea≥10%5
Upper respiratory tract infection≥10%5

Serious adverse reactions occurred in 23% of ULTOMIRIS patients vs 16% with placebo; infections were the most common serious events, including a fatal case of COVID‑19 pneumonia and one infection leading to discontinuation.5

BOXED WARNING — Meningococcal Infections: Complement inhibition with ULTOMIRIS increases the risk of serious, potentially life‑threatening Neisseria meningitidis infections. ULTOMIRIS is available only through the ULTOMIRIS REMS program, which requires prescriber enrollment and patient vaccination or antibiotic prophylaxis prior to initiation.5
